title: Stochastic optimization approaches for an operating room and anesthesiologist scheduling problem
contribution: First risk-neutral and risk-averse two-stage SP and mean-support DRO models for an integrated OR-and-anesthesiologist allocation/assignment/sequencing/scheduling problem, with MILP reformulations, a C&CG method, valid inequalities, decomposition and symmetry-breaking constraints, evaluated out of sample on public data and a New York health-system case study (arXiv v3 read).
problem_entry: Application with a named clinical partner (p. 2): existing OR models split allocation/assignment/sequencing and the closest one (Rath et al. 2017, RO) omits waiting and idle time (pp. 9-10); duration variability (Fig. 1, p. 3) and biased estimated distributions (p. 4) motivate SP and DRO.
key_idea: Dualize the moment problem (Prop. 1, p. 20), dualize the LP recourse and restrict worst-case durations to bound vertices, linearizing with McCormick and tight dual bounds (Props. 2-3, pp. 21-22), then solve by C&CG (Alg. 1, p. 24) strengthened by valid inequalities, a mean-scenario lower bound (p. 25), type-based decomposition (pp. 26-29) and symmetry-breaking (pp. 29-34).
assumptions: Known duration bounds (p. 14) and means (p. 19); fixed surgery-surgeon units (pp. 13-14); dedicated-OR/specialty policies (pp. 13, 26-27); relatively complete recourse (p. 18); identical-resource costs and same-type distributions for symmetry-breaking (pp. 29, 31-32, 34); 20th/80th percentile bounds and lognormal in-sample scenarios (p. 35).
proof_devices: moment-problem strong duality via Shapiro et al. Prop. 6.68 (p. 59)
LP dual of the recourse problem (Lemma A.2, p. 60)
separability and linearity in d_i give vertex worst case and binary program (pp. 61-62)
dual-variable bounds from complementary slackness and ordering of actual start times, shown tight by Example A.2 (pp. 63-65)
CVaR via Rockafellar-Uryasev form plus minimax swap (pp. 66-67)
exchange argument: without waiting-time terms scheduled start times are redundant and surgeries start simultaneously (Prop. A.1, pp. 56-59)
finite termination of C&CG from 2^|I| vertex scenarios (p. 24)
two-point example showing (17a) and (17b) cut different LP points (Example A.3, pp. 73-74)
experiments: Six Mannino-based instances (15-80 surgeries; Table 1, p. 35) plus six Min-Yih instances and shared-OR variants (pp. 103-111); AMPL+CPLEX 20.1, 2% gap, inexact C&CG with 600 s master limit (pp. 36-37); 20 SAA / 10 DRO replications (p. 37); ablations of VIs and symmetry-breaking (pp. 38-41, up to 145x faster); 10,000-scenario out-of-sample tests under misspecified distributions with CDFs and out-of-sample disappointment (pp. 43-47); comparisons with Rath RO, a sequential approach, extended RO and LDR (pp. 38, 46-48, 80-89); case-study sensitivity (pp. 48-51).
positioning: Claims 'first' SP/DRO models for the ORASP (p. 5); enumerated, non-polemical difference paragraphs against Wang et al. 2019, Deng et al. 2019 and Rath et al. 2017 (pp. 9-11, 19); symmetry constraints generalize ones that assume all ORs identical (pp. 30, 33); DRO placed between SP and over-conservative RO (p. 10).
writing: Numbered three-part contribution list (pp. 5-7); moderate hedging ('One possible explanation', p. 37); 'for brevity' selection of instances (pp. 38, 43); reviewer-requested analyses labelled and moved to appendix (pp. 25, 38); clinical collaborators' judgement used as the tractability bar (pp. 38, 51); small text/table mismatch in A.9.3 (pp. 88-89).
limits_future: SP-CVaR non-decomposable and unsolved on instances 5-6 (pp. 29, 37-38); variable-dependent rho bounds can slow solves (p. 26); only duration uncertainty and a mean-support set; future: emergency arrivals, block schedule and recovery units, ML duration models (p. 52).

method_links.note: One-component ablations of VIs and symmetry-breaking inside the same model; the rival RO model is given the authors' symmetry-breaking constraints 'For a fair comparison'; wins of SP at Delta = 0 and of LDR speed on instances 1-5 are printed.
In-framework extended-RO rival built only at a reviewer's request; out-of-sample tables for 2 of 6 instances 'for the sake of brevity'; CPLEX defaults, tuning effort not discussed.
Inexact C&CG (Tsang, Shehadeh, Curtis 2023) brings inexact inner solves to robust MILP, but master accuracy is a 600 s time limit, not derived from the outer loop.

Schedules judged out of sample under misspecification and by out-of-sample disappointment, not in-sample optimal value; Prop. A.1 audits the rival model's objective as rewarding non-implementable schedules.
Hard cases manufactured mechanically as misspecified distributions with supports widened by Delta, not infeasible/degenerate constraint variants.

new_pattern_candidates.pattern: degeneracy proof against the rival model
new_pattern_candidates.evidence: Prop. A.1 proves models without waiting-time terms schedule all surgeries of an anesthesiologist at once; the RO solutions are then shown to schedule all surgeries at time zero.
Solve times declared reasonable 'According to our clinical collaborators'; collaborators' preference for less packed schedules used to judge SP-E.

transferable: Mean-support DRO with LP recourse: dualize recourse, restrict worst case to bound vertices with binaries, McCormick-linearize, bound duals by complementary slackness and show tightness by example (pp. 21-22, 60-65).
Use the Dirac measure at the mean as a global lower bound and initial scenario in C&CG (p. 25).
Replace a variable-dependent valid inequality by a variable-free version when it slows the MILP, and report both (pp. 25-26).

Symmetry-breaking recipe: partition by shared resources, order identical resources by opening and load, order same-type jobs by index, keep both directional constraints for a tighter LP relaxation (pp. 29-34, 73-74).
Choose the SAA sample size by an MCO statistical gap (p. 36; pp. 111-113).

Out-of-sample protocol: in-sample family plus misspecified families with widened supports, CDFs of operational and total cost and out-of-sample disappointment, SAA-replication stability (pp. 43-47, 93-94).
coauthors: Man Yiu Tsang, Karmel S. Shehadeh, Beth Hochman, Tricia E. Brentjens
